articles.content:
How does Europe improve everyday life in border regions – and how can journalism make that impact visible? This question was at the centre of the EUconomy – Partnerships4Prosperity closing event at the newsroom of Deutsche Presse-Agentur dpa in Berlin. Representatives from the fields of European policy, academia, Interreg, the projects itself and the media discussed how the concrete results of EU cohesion policy can be communicated clearly and made relevant to regional audiences.

EU cohesion policy becomes tangible when people learn, work, access public services and cooperate across borders. This was one of the key messages of the closing event of EUconomy – Partnerships4Prosperity, a 12-month media initiative by dpa-Custom Content, co-funded by the European Union.

The event took place at the Berlin newsroom of Deutsche Presse-Agentur (dpa) and was streamed live via LinkedIn. Journalists, Interreg project coordinators, students, communication professionals and other stakeholders in European regional cooperation discussed how the impact of EU cohesion policy can be made more visible to regional audiences.

Claudius Schmidt-Faber, Senior Economic Expert at the European Commission in Germany, placed cohesion policy in the context of European integration and future regional development. Looking ahead to the EU’s next Multiannual Financial Framework from 2028, he also addressed the future architecture of cohesion policy.

“When we speak about cohesion policy, we are speaking about one of the most concrete promises of the EU: that integration should benefit all regions, territories and citizens,” Schmidt-Faber said. Europe cannot be resilient if entire regions are left behind, or united if borders remain barriers. “Cohesion is not a luxury. It is necessary.”

Interreg builds cooperation and trust

A central topic of the panel discussion was why the impact of cohesion policy is often difficult for citizens to see. Dr Kai Böhme, an expert in European regional policy and territorial development, as well as founder and director of Spatial Foresight, offered a simple explanation: “You don’t see things when they work well.” When cross-border transport, healthcare or education function smoothly, the cooperation behind them often remained invisible. The absence of obstacles could itself be a result of successful cohesion policy, Böhme added.

Izabela Glišić, Head of the Joint Secretariat of the Interreg VI A Brandenburg-Poland 2021-2027 Cooperation Programme, emphasised that Interreg was fundamentally about funding cooperation between regions and countries. A central focus was building trust, creating relationships that can continue beyond individual funding projects.

Interreg supports regions in addressing challenges in areas including innovation, mobility, healthcare, climate adaptation, emergency services and education. “Interreg is not only about funding projects. It is about building habits of cooperation,” said Schmidt-Faber. “It creates trust – and in today’s Europe, trust is a strategic asset.”

TRAIL: Cohesion policy in higher education

Pinar Hepperle, Coordinator of the Sustainable Business Development Master’s programme at Offenburg University, contributed the project perspective. The Interreg-funded TRAIL project connects universities in Offenburg, Strasbourg and Basel. Students gain international and practical experience and prepare for a sustainable, cross-border working environment.

TRAIL shows how EU cohesion policy can connect students, universities, companies and the regional labour market. Hepperle also highlighted a key communication challenge: projects need to be explained differently to different audiences – including students, companies interested in cooperation, the wider public and administrative stakeholders. Effective communication therefore requires different approaches and formats rather than one single message, she said.

The discussion underlined that reporting on EU-funded projects should go beyond funding figures and institutional language. The key questions are concrete: Who benefits? What has changed? Which regional challenge is being addressed? And why was cross-border cooperation necessary?

© Annette Riedl

About EUconomy

EUconomy – Partnerships4Prosperity is a 12-month media initiative by dpa-Custom Content, co-funded by the European Union. The project produces free multimedia content packages – including videos, images and social media material – documenting EU-funded cross-border projects in Germany’s border regions with Austria, Poland, the Czech Republic, France and Denmark. All content is made available free of charge to media outlets across Germany and beyond.

dpa is the lead agency coordinating the European Newsroom (enr), a network of European news agencies.

Press contact: euconomy-pressevent@dpa.com

articles.personality_title: EU cohesion policy strengthens cooperation and daily life in border regions
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – The European Union (EU) works to improve life in regions near country borders by supporting cooperation between them. This effort is called cohesion policy, and it helps people access jobs, education, healthcare, and other services across borders. A project called EUconomy – Partnerships4Prosperity has been sharing stories about how this policy makes a difference.

**What happened** – In June 2024, the EUconomy project held a closing event at the Deutsche Presse-Agentur newsroom in Berlin. Experts from the EU, universities, media, and regional cooperation programs like Interreg talked about how to explain the real benefits of EU cohesion policy to local communities. They shared examples like cross-border transport and education programs that work smoothly because of EU support.

**Impact** – The event showed that cohesion policy is more than money—it builds trust and connections between regions that last beyond individual projects. For example, the TRAIL project links universities in Germany, France, and Switzerland, helping students gain international experience and prepare for jobs across borders. Experts explained that when services run well, people might not notice the cooperation behind them, which is why good communication is important.

**What's next step** – The EU will continue funding cohesion policy through its next long-term budget starting in 2028. Media and project leaders plan to improve how they share stories so more people understand who benefits from these programs and why cross-border cooperation matters. This could help strengthen regional ties and support future projects.

**One-sentence takeaway** – EU cohesion policy helps border regions work together and improve daily life by building trust, sharing resources, and connecting people across countries.
articles.personality_title_fr: La politique de cohésion de l’UE renforce la coopération et la vie quotidienne dans les régions frontalières
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – L’Union européenne (UE) œuvre à améliorer la vie dans les régions proches des frontières en soutenant la coopération entre elles. Cette démarche s’appelle la politique de cohésion et elle aide les habitants à accéder à l’emploi, à l’éducation, aux soins de santé et à d’autres services au-delà des frontières. Un projet nommé EUconomy – Partnerships4Prosperity partage des histoires montrant l’impact positif de cette politique.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – En juin 2024, le projet EUconomy a organisé un événement de clôture au siège de l’agence Deutsche Presse-Agentur à Berlin. Des experts de l’UE, des universités, des médias et des programmes de coopération régionale comme Interreg ont discuté de la meilleure façon d’expliquer aux communautés locales les bénéfices concrets de la politique de cohésion. Ils ont donné des exemples comme les transports transfrontaliers et les programmes éducatifs qui fonctionnent grâce au soutien de l’UE.

**Impact** – L’événement a montré que la politique de cohésion est plus qu’un financement : elle crée de la confiance et des liens durables entre les régions. Par exemple, le projet TRAIL relie des universités en Allemagne, en France et en Suisse, aidant les étudiants à acquérir une expérience internationale et à se préparer à travailler au-delà des frontières. Les experts ont expliqué que lorsque les services fonctionnent bien, les habitants ne voient pas toujours la coopération qui les soutient, d’où l’importance d’une bonne communication.

**Prochaine étape** – L’UE continuera de financer la politique de cohésion dans son prochain budget à long terme à partir de 2028. Les médias et les responsables de projets prévoient d’améliorer la manière de raconter ces histoires pour que davantage de personnes comprennent qui bénéficie de ces programmes et pourquoi la coopération transfrontalière est importante. Cela pourrait renforcer les liens régionaux et soutenir de futurs projets.

**Résumé en une phrase** – La politique de cohésion de l’UE aide les régions frontalières à collaborer et à améliorer la vie quotidienne en créant la confiance, en partageant les ressources et en reliant les habitants au-delà des frontières.
articles.personality_title_es: La política de cohesión de la UE fortalece la cooperación y la vida diaria en regiones fronterizas
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – La Unión Europea (UE) trabaja para mejorar la vida en las regiones cercanas a las fronteras apoyando la cooperación entre ellas. Este esfuerzo se llama política de cohesión y ayuda a las personas a acceder a empleos, educación, atención médica y otros servicios a través de las fronteras. Un proyecto llamado EUconomy – Partnerships4Prosperity ha estado compartiendo historias sobre cómo esta política hace una diferencia.

**Qué pasó** – En junio de 2024, el proyecto EUconomy realizó un evento de clausura en la redacción de Deutsche Presse-Agentur en Berlín. Expertos de la UE, universidades, medios y programas de cooperación regional como Interreg hablaron sobre cómo explicar mejor los beneficios reales de la política de cohesión a las comunidades locales. Compartieron ejemplos como el transporte y la educación transfronterizos que funcionan bien gracias al apoyo de la UE.

**Impacto** – El evento mostró que la política de cohesión es más que dinero: construye confianza y conexiones entre regiones que duran más allá de proyectos individuales. Por ejemplo, el proyecto TRAIL conecta universidades en Alemania, Francia y Suiza, ayudando a estudiantes a obtener experiencia internacional y prepararse para trabajos en diferentes países. Los expertos explicaron que cuando los servicios funcionan bien, las personas a veces no ven la cooperación detrás, por eso la comunicación es importante.

**Próximo paso** – La UE seguirá financiando la política de cohesión en su próximo presupuesto a largo plazo a partir de 2028. Los medios y líderes de proyectos planean mejorar cómo cuentan estas historias para que más personas entiendan quién se beneficia y por qué importa la cooperación transfronteriza. Esto podría fortalecer los lazos regionales y apoyar futuros proyectos.

**Frase clave** – La política de cohesión de la UE ayuda a las regiones fronterizas a trabajar juntas y mejorar la vida diaria al construir confianza, compartir recursos y conectar a las personas entre países.
